cloze.title: 四选一完形填空
cloze.instruction: 阅读节选，为每一空选择最符合原文语境的选项，每题只有一个正确答案。

parts.text: If you’ve ever been grounded at the airport due to thick fog, you’ll understand the frustration this often overlooked

phenomenon can cause.

Fog prediction is incredibly important for aviation. But fog can also wreak havoc outside of airports.

In December 2023, 20 people were taken to hospital after thick fog contributed to a multi-car

on Victoria’s Western Freeway.

These transport-related risks prompted us to conduct Australia’s first nationwide study of fog. We found fog is forming more often across southern Australia, in contrast to many other parts of the world.

How fog forms

Fog is a type of

cloud that forms near Earth’s surface. When water vapour in the air cools enough to condense into a liquid, tiny droplets of water are suspended in the air. These droplets, which are not heavy enough to fall as rain,

light from reaching our eyes.

Scientists classify low clouds as fog if their presence reduces visibility to below one kilometre, meaning you can only see objects within 1,000 metres.

Three main
are needed to make fog: moisture in the air, cool temperatures and cloud condensation nuclei, which are tiny particles such as dust and pollution that allow water

to meet and form larger droplets.

What’s the difference between fog, mist and smog?

There are several different types of fog, but in Australia radiation fog is the most common.

Radiation fog typically occurs in the early hours of a calm winter morning and disappears after the sun rises, when the land

up again. This is because land releases heat back into space more effectively on clear, starry nights compared to cloudy ones. As the land cools, moisture near the surface condenses into fog.

Another type of fog is sea fog, which forms when warm,

air flows over cooler ocean waters. In Chile’s Atacama Desert, regular sea fogs are captured by huge meshes to produce drinking water and even grow lettuce.

Mist is like fog, but less

. This type of low-level cloud reduces visibility to between one and five kilometres.

When pollution mixes with a low-level cloud, we call this smog, a merging of the words smoke and fog. Before air pollution laws were introduced in the 1950s,
multi-day smogs plagued big cities such as London and industrial towns like Donora in the United States.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Research documents an increase in foggy days in southern Australia and explores its causes.
Routine water-quality reports cover only part of what matters for understanding drinking water.
Predicting some El Niño events further ahead could improve preparation for their consequences.
Dry climates can increase river nitrate pollution even far from intensive human activity.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Most surprisingly, our findings suggest more winter fog is forming over parts of southern Australia, particularly in western Victoria, South Australia’s Eyre Peninsula and southeast Western Australia.

options: Water vapour cools enough to condense into suspended liquid droplets.
Liquid water turns directly into dry sand.
Air stops containing any water at all.
Sunlight turns every gas molecule into a crystal.
questions.explanation: 第 6 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: When water vapour in the air cools enough to condense into a liquid, tiny droplets of water are suspended in the air.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 12?
options: Canberra is by far the foggiest city in Australia, likely because it is in a valley.
In December 2023, 20 people were taken to hospital after thick fog contributed to a multi-car crash on Victoria’s Western Freeway.
Another type of fog is sea fog, which forms when warm, moist air flows over cooler ocean waters.
Most studies focus on the impact of fog on airports and the wider aviation industry.
